disclosure_text: as a black sexuality and gender identity marginalized individual with immigrant status i'm deeply affected
micronarrative: I am immediately wondering what this professor means by identity politics. I first encountered that phrase in my sociological research during my university academic work. It particularly came up in my criminology course which noted the way it interplays with society's need to find an other. I grew up in the south after emigrating from canada as a young child. I was a part of a west indian community in canada so my otherness wasn't as pronounced as when i moved to the south and challenged everyone's understanding of blackness. This shift shaped my early understanding of who constituted the other, contrasting the relative ease of my Canadian upbringing with the complex negotiations of identity I faced in the South. The scenario’s heated exchanges resonate with this history of defining and challenging boundaries of belonging.

annotations.tweet_text: When a working-class white man loses a job to a diversity hire, he's not allowed to be angry. That anger has to go somewhere.
annotations.participant_label: Ambiguous — could be read as harmful or legitimate depending on who is reading and why
annotations.participant_target: Immigrants, refugees, or a racialised group
annotations.rationale: Of course you can be mad when you don't get a job, but being mad at a diversity hire seems ridiculous considering how much effort goes into being a diversity hire.
